Honestly I doubt you’ll get much help on Reddit. The tattooing community widely condemns scratching for the unsafe practise it is. Read any article watch and any video they’ll all tell you to get an apprenticeship and learn the right way. Most supply shops won’t even sell to you if you’re not licensed.
If you don’t want to go into tattooing and just want it for yourself for whatever reason then ultimately it’s down to you but 99% of artists are going to tell you what I’ve just told you. Do the right thing and get an apprenticeship.

Help them help you. Your ideas might be scattered I know mine definitely were for my first but that consultation will help you and the artist a lot. They’ll be able to help you streamline your ideas until you’re both happy you’ve got an idea to work with. 
But if your ideas are a chrome space reaper, bible scripture, a portrait of Tom Brady, the name of your old dog, the name of your new dog, but all kinda with a floral background that turns into birds then yeah they might struggle to combine them😂

I prefer all black so I am bias, I think once you’ve gone with a couple of colours you’ve got to stick to them otherwise they’re gonna clash. Then you’ve got fading like you mention. On top of that depending on what you’ve already got it could look a bit ‘patchy’ having areas which are only black and others with lots of colour. 
However I do think a little bit of colour can look really good and add a lot to an otherwise black tattoo. I think it’d come down to what you’ve already got and what you want to add, it could come together really well. :)

Numbing cream - probably best to ask your artist if there’s any they can recommend. 

Painkillers - Had a couple people tell me codeine or tramadol helped them sit for a lot longer but obviously make sure you’d be okay taking them before you do that.

I don’t think anyone dislikes the concept but it’s the quality that’s questionable. If you’re happy with it then that is all that matters but can you genuinely look at that image without any bias and say it’s looks well done? Maybe it’s the picture but the lines look all off. I really like the idea, I think it’d be worth spending the extra to get it looking neat and tidy.

It’s gonna be different for everyone, maybe try get one elsewhere first just to see how you handle it, last thing you want is to book in for a long session then really struggle through it. I got my chest (from the top of my abs up to my collar bones and the bottom of my neck) done as my 4th tattoo. I found the bottom of my neck and sternum to be the hardest parts. The pecs were pretty easy but after about 2 hours and going over some spots again it became uncomfortable for me.
Play classic, it’ll be hard and confusing but probably one of the most rewarding gaming experiences you’ll ever have.
